diagnosis.summary: Counted tracks show north-south through and related turning activity with high share of time stopped, suggesting north-south load or turning interaction as possible limits, but key entering flows are withheld and per-movement and stopped-share values lack independent validation, so measurement artefact remains a competing explanation.

hypotheses.statement: Operation is limited by heavy north-south through demand, with the N-S and S-N through movements dominating the validated turn counts and producing high stopped time.
hypotheses.how_to_check: Obtain an independent on-road classified count by arm and movement over the same period with manual validation of queues, plus signal state logs, to confirm whether north-south through demand is the main load and source of stopped time.

hypotheses.statement: Operation is limited by turning friction where N-E left and S-E right flows interact with opposing through flows, creating stops disproportionate to through volume alone.
hypotheses.how_to_check: Measure lane-specific arrivals, turning queues and discharge interactions on the road with signal state, to test whether left and right turning flows conflict with through flows.

hypotheses.statement: The apparent pattern reflects computer-vision limits rather than a true operational limit, with missed stopped vehicles, mid-view starts retained in totals and turns, coarse arm quadrants and window cut-off distorting the distribution and stopped share.
hypotheses.how_to_check: Repeat counting with independent on-road manual counts and tracked queue observations that capture stopped vehicles and window-edge effects, with per-movement validation, to test whether the apparent dominance and stopped share persist.

limitations: Entering flow and entering counts by arm were withheld and cannot be used to infer demand, capacity or balance.
No signal timing, phasing, saturation flow, queue length or delay-cause data are in evidence, so stopped time cannot be attributed to a signal or bottleneck.
Ground positions are approximate and along-road distances are not accepted; speed agreement when moving is empirical and not a calibrated speed measurement.
Arms and turns are coarse quadrants from first and last track points; a track cut off by the window has no exit and no turn.
Counted totals include mid-view starts that are either restarted tracks or queued vehicles first seen moving, while entering definitions exclude them.
The detector misses some stopped vehicles on visual check and some track points are interpolated across missed detections, so stopped share and totals are uncertain.
Turning agreement was checked pooled and not movement by movement, so no single movement count is individually validated.
Vehicle classes without a detector label are inferred from rough size and boxes and tracks are not ground truth with no value measured on the road.
Footage is historical and from a different city and period than the present junction operation, and part of the image is window frame with flagged points.

diagnosis.summary: Tracks suggest operation centred on north-south through movements with substantial stopped time and a notable north to east left movement within a car-dominated fleet, with detector misses and coarse movement definitions limiting certainty.

hypotheses.statement: Junction operation is limited by heavy north to south and south to north through demand relative to east and west movements.
hypotheses.how_to_check: Collect independent on-road manual classified counts by movement with simultaneous signal state logging and queue observation on the same approaches to verify relative through demand.

hypotheses.statement: Junction operation is limited by queuing and delay reflected in a high share of time stopped.
hypotheses.how_to_check: Measure on-road queue lengths, stopped time and discharge behaviour with independent signal state records to determine whether stopped time reflects signal-related queuing.

hypotheses.statement: Junction operation is limited by friction between the north to east left movement and opposing north-south through flow.
hypotheses.how_to_check: Obtain lane-resolved on-road observations of left-turn arrivals, opposing through flow and yielding and blocking behaviour to test whether the north to east left movement interacts with through flow.

hypotheses.statement: Junction operation is limited by volume of cars rather than by heavy-vehicle composition, with cars dominating counted tracks.
hypotheses.how_to_check: Undertake independent on-road classified counts with verified vehicle dimensions to confirm fleet mix and whether heavy vehicles contribute to operational limitation.

limitations: This evidence cannot show signal timing or phase operation, so stopped time cannot be attributed to signal control from this evidence alone.
This evidence cannot show entering flow or totals by arm because those values were withheld and must not be inferred.
This evidence cannot show reliable movement-level turning volumes on its own because turning agreement was checked pooled and arms and turns are coarse quadrants with window-cut tracks lacking exits.

This evidence cannot show full demand or stopped-vehicle exposure because the detector missed stopped vehicles on visual check and tracks beginning mid-view were excluded from entering counts while retained elsewhere.
This evidence cannot show calibrated speed or along-road distance because ground positions rely on an approximated homography with only empirical agreement for moving speed.
This evidence cannot show fleet mix with certainty because classes without a detector label were inferred from rough size and tracks include interpolation and fragments.

diagnosis.summary: Overhead tracking shows many counted tracks dominated by cars with north-south through movements and eastward turns present, alongside substantial stopped time while movement when moving remains at the gated value.

hypotheses.statement: Junction operation is limited mainly by high demand for through travel between north and south arms.
hypotheses.how_to_check: Separate independent counts of approach demand and exit service by arm from on-road observation over multiple signal cycles, with turning movements recorded independently.

hypotheses.statement: Junction operation is limited mainly by time spent stopped due to signal control or queuing rather than by moving conditions.
hypotheses.how_to_check: Independent measurement of queue formation and discharge by approach from roadside observation, together with direct recording of signal states.

hypotheses.statement: Junction operation is limited mainly by turning interactions toward the east arm from north and south entries.
hypotheses.how_to_check: Independent observation of turning paths and conflict area occupancy, with separate recording of turning versus through queues by approach.

limitations: Withheld entering flow and arm entry values cannot be used to infer demand or balance.
Movement counts were checked only pooled, so no single movement count is independently validated on its own.
The detector misses some stopped vehicles and some tracks begin mid-view and are excluded from entering counts, so entering demand can run low while totals mix different track types.

Positions come from an approximated camera mapping with along-road distances not accepted, speed is shown only as gated agreement and not as calibrated measurement, and some points are interpolated with short fragments excluded from counts.
Vehicle classes without detector labels are inferred from rough size, and arms and turns are coarse quadrants with window-cut tracks lacking exit and turn.
No signal timing, lane layout, priority, pedestrian, or downstream condition information is present in the evidence.
